title: MaverIQ: Fingerprint-Guided Extrapolation and Fragmentation-Aware Layering for Intent-Based LLM Serving
problem: Deploying LLMs optimally requires manual exploration of parallelism/compression configurations; existing solutions rely on expensive profiling and suboptimally utilize fragmented cluster resources
method: Fingerprint-based extrapolation: profile small LLM proxy under few configs, analytically extrapolate to full model; fragmentation-aware layering exploits uneven layer distribution for cost optimization

title: An 8.62μW 75dB-DR SoC End-to-End Spoken-Language-Understanding SoC With Channel-Level AGC and Temporal-Sparsity-Aware Streaming-Mode RNN
problem: Voice-controlled IoT and wearable devices require ultra-low-power always-on audio classification for continuous speech input (not just single-word) with >60dB input range to handle variable speech volume. Prior designs either used costly analog front-ends (>50% of power) or analog feature extractors that couldn't achieve both low power and high accuracy on multi-class tasks with variable input levels.
method: The design integrates channel-level automatic gain control (AGC) with a temporal-sparsity-aware streaming-mode RNN for end-to-end SLU. The AGC handles the >60dB input dynamic range while the streaming RNN exploits temporal sparsity in speech signals to reduce computation. Full system integration on a single SoC combines analog front-end processing with digital RNN inference.

title: An elastic job scheduler for HPC applications on the cloud
problem: Cloud's pay-as-you-go model requires efficient resource utilization. Traditional parallel programming models (MPI) don't support autoscaling. HPC on cloud needs dynamic rescaling to match resource availability and minimize cost.
method: Kubernetes operator for Charm++ applications on Kubernetes. Priority-based elastic job scheduler dynamically rescales jobs based on cluster state. Optimizes for resource utilization and response time for high-priority jobs.

title: RAGO: Systematic Performance Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Serving
problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) serving is emerging as a critical LLM deployment pattern, but diverse RAG algorithm variants exhibit wildly different workload characteristics (retrieval latency, reranking compute, generation length), making a single optimization strategy inadequate. There is no systematic framework for characterizing and optimizing across the space of RAG pipelines.
method: RAGO introduces RAGSchema, a structured abstraction encoding the components and dataflow of any RAG algorithm, used to characterize and compare workload behaviors. The paper analyzes representative RAG variants with distinct schemas, exposing performance bottlenecks. RAGO then applies algorithm-specific system optimizations—scheduling policies, resource partitioning, and batching strategies—tuned to each RAGSchema's profile, rather than treating all RAG variants uniformly as extended LLM inference workloads.

title: FLAG: An FPGA-Based System for Low-Latency GNN Inference Service Using Vector Quantization
problem: Real-time GNN inference serving faces two bottlenecks: intensive preparation (neighbor aggregation, feature computation) and the neighborhood explosion problem (exponential neighbor set growth across layers), making it difficult to meet low end-to-end latency service level agreements.
method: FLAG offloads preparation to offline preprocessing, precomputing and compressing hidden embeddings via vector quantization. A dedicated FPGA accelerator ingests the precomputed data and performs lightweight online aggregation using the compressed embeddings, eliminating repeated computation.

title: Dynamic Thread Coarsening for CPU and GPU OpenMP Code
problem: Thread coarsening is well-known for GPU optimization but less explored for CPUs. Divergent control flow reduces effectiveness on both platforms. Existing approaches require compile-time uniformity proof, limiting applicability to real programs with data-dependent control flow.
method: Implement multi-level thread coarsening for CPU and GPU OpenMP code via generic LLVM IR transformation. Introduce dynamic convergence: generate both coarsened and non-coarsened code paths for divergent regions; runtime decision based on thread uniformity. Evaluate on HecBench (GPU) and LULESH (CPU).

title: 32.3 An Accurate Secondary-Side Controller with GaN-Based CGS Isolated Driver Achieving Sub-1% Error On-Chip Sensing
problem: LLC resonant converter secondary-side controllers require precise synchronous-rectifier (SR) on/off timing to minimize dead-time losses; conventional GaN SRs lack body diodes and suffer from current-collapse effects, and accurate current sensing at the secondary side is difficult to integrate.
method: A secondary-side controller with GaN-based common-gate-source (CGS) isolated driver enabling accurate on-chip current sensing via a gate-charge (CGS) monitoring technique. The driver provides strong driving capability with zero delay and precise SR timing while maintaining integrated current-sensing accuracy below 1% error.

title: Quartz: A Reconfigurable, Distributed-Memory Accelerator for Sparse Applications
problem: Sparse tensor and graph workloads exhibit irregular memory access patterns and variable computation densities that defeat fixed-dataflow ASIC accelerators designed for dense workloads. No single dataflow or memory organization handles the full diversity of sparse application kernels efficiently.
method: Quartz is a reconfigurable ASIC accelerator with distributed on-chip SRAM banks. The architecture exposes a programmable dataflow substrate that can be configured at runtime to match the access pattern of a given sparse kernel. Distributed memory banks reduce the bandwidth bottleneck by providing high aggregate internal bandwidth close to the compute units. A reconfigurable interconnect routes data between memory banks and processing elements according to the configured dataflow.

title: FRoZN: Fault-Tolerant Routing Technique Using Reinforcement Learning for ZMesh NoC
problem: Fault-tolerant NoC routing faces dynamic network conditions and inefficient fault recovery
method: Q-learning reinforcement learning on ZMesh NoC (hybrid mesh+zigzag topology) for dynamic fault-adaptive routing

title: Determining Levels of Detail for Simulators of Parallel and Distributed Computing Systems via Automated Calibration
problem: Simulator accuracy depends on level of detail AND parameter calibration; trade-off between accuracy and complexity
method: Automated calibration framework; methodology for picking simulator detail levels; two case studies

title: Revisiting Reliability in Large-Scale Machine Learning Research Clusters
problem: Large-scale ML training clusters suffer from frequent job failures whose impact on training efficiency is not well characterized across different job sizes and cluster configurations. Existing failure models do not adequately capture workload diversity or provide actionable metrics like Effective Training Time Ratio (ETTR).
method: The authors conducted an 11-month observational study across two large multi-tenant A100 GPU clusters totaling 4 million jobs and over 150 million GPU-hours. They developed a failure taxonomy, computed Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) as a function of GPU count by fitting a failure model to operational data, and derived an analytical estimator for Effective Training Time Ratio (ETTR) as a function of job parameters (checkpoint interval, restart overhead, failure rate). The ETTR model is used to project the efficacy of software mitigations such as more frequent checkpointing.

title: The (R)evolution of Scientific Workflows in the Agentic AI Era: Towards Autonomous Science
problem: Modern scientific discovery requires coordinating distributed facilities and heterogeneous resources. Researchers act as manual workflow coordinators rather than scientists, limiting discovery velocity and scalability.
method: Propose a conceptual framework charting workflow evolution along two dimensions: intelligence (static to intelligent) and composition (single to swarm). Present architectural blueprint for autonomous, distributed scientific laboratories.

title: Leopard: Hardware Pass-Through Remote Storage Access with Queue Concurrency for Edge Intelligent Workstations
problem: Edge workstations access remote cloud storage via complex software stacks and limited CPUs, causing 75% performance degradation by failing to saturate NVMe queue concurrency.
method: Leopard implements a custom NVMe controller on SmartNIC FPGA that emulates NVMe device and directly handles remote storage operations via parallelized hardware circuits; passes NVMe commands directly from edge OS to FPGA, bypassing CPU stacks.

title: Late Breaking Results: FPGen-3D: Automated Framework for 3D-FPGA Architecture Generation and Exploration
problem: FPGA design space exploration is limited by 2D constraints; exploring 3D FPGA architectures with vertical connections requires manual and tedious design efforts, preventing efficient navigation of 3D design space.
method: FPGen-3D automates 3D FPGA architecture generation from user-defined parameters, producing synthesizable RTL, routing results, and programming bitstreams. Explores vertical connection strategies via 3D switch blocks (SB) and 3D configurable logic blocks (CLB).

title: LegoZK: A Dynamically Reconfigurable Accelerator for Zero-Knowledge Proof
problem: Existing ZKP accelerators are designed at the granularity of core operators and exhibit low hardware resource utilization and limited adaptability across the different computation stages of proof generation (e.g., NTT, MSM, polynomial operations).
method: LegoZK uses finite field arithmetic units (FAUs) as fundamental building blocks integrated via a hierarchical on-chip NoC. By dynamically configuring the FAUs and the NoC interconnect at runtime, LegoZK can target each computation stage of proof generation without hardware specialization per stage. For the most time-consuming stage (Multi-Scalar Multiplication, MSM), LegoZK proposes a fast, fully pipelined bucket reduction algorithm based on lookup tables, significantly reducing MSM latency. The NoC topology and FAU configuration are switched between proof stages.

title: Fine-grained Automated Failure Management for Extreme-Scale GPU Accelerated Systems
problem: As HPC systems scale, hardware failure rates increase; mean time to repair (MTTR) becomes critical bottleneck, with MTBF decreasing for GPU-accelerated systems
method: Centralized meta-database tracking event history with correlated event analysis; fine-grained multi-strike repair policies; automated recovery framework deployed on Aurora supercomputer
